title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In (1.6) the right-hand side for u^4 a4' is written (per transcription, and seemingly in the typescript) as -F(r,t) - s F_t(r,t). Direct expansion gives a4 - s a3 + 2 a2 r - (t+rs) a1 + 3r^2 - 2st = -F_x(r,t) - s F_y(r,t). The first term should therefore be the partial derivative -F_r(r,t) (= -F_x(r,t)), not -F(r,t); a subscript is missing.

No other errors found. I checked the second expression for Delta, all of (1.6) and (1.7), the discriminant remarks (c4, 16 Delta), and the d6 transformation exactly. For d8 I checked the linear term in r (it gives -c6) but did not verify that the higher-order terms in r vanish.

ideas.what: Tate's Weierstrass invariants a_i, b_i, c4, c6, Delta and their transformation laws under x = u^2x'+r, y = u^3y'+su^2x'+t
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Tate (circulated c. 1965), written up by P. Deligne, 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', LNM 476 (1975)
ideas.where_published: Deligne's Formulaire (Antwerp IV); Silverman AEC III.1

ideas.what: Expressing a3', a4', a6' via F and its partials at (r,t)
ideas.modern_name: Taylor expansion of the Weierstrass polynomial at the new origin

ideas.what: Semi-invariants d6, d8 with u^6 d6' = d6 + c4 r and u^8 d8' = d8 - c6 r, with 12 d6 = c6 + b2 c4 and -12 d8 = c4^2 + b2 c6
ideas.modern_name: Ramanujan/Serre derivative of c4, c6; b2 as an E2-like (quasi-modular) coordinate in the Gauss–Manin connection on the de Rham bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1916) for the q-expansion identities; N. Katz (1973, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms', appendix; 1976 on real-analytic Eisenstein series) for the algebraic Gauss–Manin version
ideas.where_published: Katz, Antwerp III (LNM 350); later Movasati's 'Gauss–Manin connection in disguise'

ideas.what: Discriminants of the r-polynomials (c4 and 16 Delta); the 2-division polynomial

missed.claim: The notes record explicit polynomial semi-invariants d6, d8 that transform affinely under the r-translation. They are tied to c4, c6 by the Ramanujan-type identities 12 d6 = c6 + b2 c4 and -12 d8 = c4^2 + b2 c6, set up as a prelude to the Gauss–Manin connection. This is an early, purely algebraic Weierstrass-coordinate version of the quasi-modular/Ramanujan structure. It anticipates the 'Gauss–Manin connection in disguise' viewpoint, but the content is known (Katz 1973) and the typescript is likely not by Grothendieck himself.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of documentary interest: it shows how the Montpellier circle organised the Weierstrass formulaire around a b2-translation (E2-like) parameter to compute Picard–Fuchs equations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is essentially Tate's standard formulaire, correctly computed apart from a missing partial-derivative subscript. The only slightly unusual items are the semi-invariants d6, d8 encoding Ramanujan-type derivative relations, which are known in substance (Katz) and likely not Grothendieck's own.
transcription_corrections: In the u^4 a4' line, the typescript's '-F(r,t)' should mathematically be '-F_r(r,t)' (partial derivative); either a typescript slip or a dropped subscript.
'F_t' denotes the partial derivative with respect to the second variable (y), evaluated at (r,t).
